title: AT-AT: Automatic Tool Optimization from Agent Traces
abstract: arXiv:2610.34679v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Efforts to improve LLM-based agents typically focus on modifying the agent itself, yet success also depends on the environment in which an agent acts. Tools mediate this interaction: a tool's description shapes how an agent calls it, and its implementation determines the results and errors the agent receives afterwards. Many tools, such as APIs and MCP servers, are shared by many agents and maintained by providers who cannot change those agents. We introduce AT-AT (Automatic Tool Optimization from Agent Traces), an agentic tool optimizer that improves a shared toolset offline from historical agent executions while holding the agents fixed. A lightweight coding agent reads agent trajectories and their evaluation results, and selectively edits tool descriptions and, when permitted, implementations. translated_title: AT-AT：基于智能体轨迹的自动工具优化
translated_abstract: 提升基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体的研究通常集中于修改智能体本身，然而成功还取决于智能体所处的运行环境。工具在其中起到中介作用：工具的描述决定了智能体如何调用它，而工具的实现则决定了智能体随后收到的结果与错误信息。许多工具（如 API 和 MCP 服务器）被多个智能体共享，并由无法修改这些智能体的提供者维护。我们提出了 AT-AT（Automatic Tool Optimization from Agent Traces，基于智能体轨迹的自动工具优化），这是一种智能体式的工具优化器，能够在保持智能体不变的前提下，从历史智能体执行记录中离线改进共享工具集。一个轻量级的编码智能体读取智能体轨迹及其评估结果，并有选择地编辑工具描述，以及在允许的情况下编辑工具实现。在 τ²-bench-verified 基准上，AT-AT 在 Airline 和 Telecom 领域以更低的成本取得了最高的任务完成率，优于强提示基线方法。
tldr: 提出 AT-AT 方法，通过轻量级编码智能体分析历史智能体执行轨迹，在不修改智能体的情况下离线自动优化共享工具的描述与实现，从而以更低成本显著提升任务完成率。
en_tdlr: AT-AT uses a lightweight coding agent to automatically optimize shared tool descriptions and implementations offline from historical agent traces, achieving higher task completion rates at lower cost without modifying the agents themselves.
